source: Oyserman and Lee (2008) Does culture influence what and how we think? Effects of priming individualism and collectivism, Psychological Bulletin 134
finding: Human baseline for the whole subfield. Priming individualism vs collectivism has a small-to-moderate average effect, mostly on relationality and cognition.
numbers: 67 studies, 6,240 participants, 369 effect sizes. Mean weighted d = 0.34 (95% CI 0.29-0.39; Z=12.90); mean unweighted d = 0.45. Dropping 3 anomalous studies (64 studies, 5,408 people): weighted d = 0.42 (CI 0.37-0.48). Rosenthal fail-safe N = 3,495.
limits: Almost all samples were undergraduates. Priming-induced effects are lab effects on short tasks. Authors say effects are small to moderate, d mostly 0.3 to 0.6.
agent_relevance: The human anchor: a cue can move style, but by about a third to a half of a standard deviation, not a switch. An agent cue should be expected to give a partial, not total, shift.

source: Oyserman and Lee (2008), publication-bias and prime-type moderators
finding: Trim-and-fill added 24 imagined missing studies and the effect shrank but stayed above zero. Which prime is used matters a lot. Language as the prime was weakest (about d = 0).
numbers: Adjusted weighted d = 0.17 (CI 0.12-0.21) after imputing 24 studies. Prime task QB = 47.48, p < .001: SDFF d = 0.49 (n=10); Sumerian warrior d = 0.45; scrambled sentence d = 0.32 (n=7 by table order; table text is garbled in extraction); group imagination about 0.34. Priming both relational and group collectivism d = 0.52 (n=22) vs group only 0.28 (n=11) vs relational only 0.39 (n=28).
limits: Table columns in the PDF text extraction are partly scrambled, so the per-task mapping of d to task name should be checked against the printed table.
agent_relevance: Priming by changing the language of the task was the weakest human cue. Rich, content-based cues (think about what you share with others) worked better than a surface language switch. Relevant to prompt-language versus persona cues for LLMs.

source: Oyserman and Lee (2008), outcome and region moderators
finding: Effect size depends on what is measured. Relationality and cognition moderate; values and self-concept small. East-West differences in the priming effect are partly explained by task choices.
numbers: Relationality d = 0.61; cognition d = 0.54; values d = 0.29; self-concept d = 0.26; well-being near zero or negative. Cognition subtypes: social attitudes d = 0.50 (n=10), social comparison d = 0.59 (n=10), nonsocial judgments (memory, visual perception) d = 0.52 (n=8); QB = 0.91, p = .63. In the East 60% of studies used group-level primes (small effects) and 40% used language as the prime.
limits: Region and language are confounded. Cognition outcomes are mixed social and nonsocial tasks, so this is not a pure test of analytic versus holistic style.
agent_relevance: The cognitive-style effect (d about 0.5) is the part most relevant to a reasoning scaffold, and it holds for nonsocial judgments too.

source: Jin, Zhang, Shu, Cui (2023) The Cultural Psychology of Large Language Models: Is ChatGPT a Holistic or Analytic Thinker?
finding: Gave GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 four cultural-psychology scales. On cognitive-process scales (Analysis-Holism Scale, triadic categorization) both models looked holistic, like East Asians. On value scales (dialectical self, self-construal) there was no clear lean.
numbers: 10 runs per model at temperature 1. AHS: GPT-3.5 M=5.35 (SD 0.11), GPT-4 M=5.01 (SD 0.10) vs human norm 4.87 (SD 0.49, N=702). Dialectical Self Scale: GPT-3.5 4.59 vs norm 4.00; GPT-4 3.97, p = .344 (no difference). Self-construal independent: GPT-3.5 6.98, GPT-4 5.32 vs norm 4.73; interdependent: GPT-3.5 5.85, GPT-4 4.95 vs norm 4.81 (p = .07). Triadic categorization score 0.87 (GPT-3.5), 0.85 (GPT-4), above most Chinese provinces.
limits: Only 10 runs per cell, so t-tests against human norms treat run-to-run variance as if it were between-person variance. No priming manipulation was applied. Authors admit no prompt-design or fine-tuning tests.
agent_relevance: Default LLM style is already tilted holistic on style scales and is not a blank slate. Any cue test must start from this baseline.

source: Jin et al. (2023), robustness section
finding: Changing temperature and changing the language of the prompt did not change the main pattern, per the authors.
numbers: Only shown in a figure (Figure 1); no numbers in text. At temperature 0 the SD is zero.
limits: The claim of robustness rests on a figure, not tabulated tests. Later work (c08-c10) finds language effects can be weak or reversed.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence that a surface cue (prompt language) moves the baseline for the 2023 GPT models.

source: PsyPost report of Lu, Song, Zhang (2025) Cultural tendencies in generative AI, Nature Human Behaviour (doi 10.1038/s41562-025-02242-1)
finding: Primary LLM paper on prompt-language priming. GPT-4 and ERNIE 3.5 answered the same measures in English and Chinese. Chinese gave more interdependent social orientation and more holistic cognitive style. Tasks: attribution bias, syllogisms, expectation of change. Slogan test: Chinese prompts favored interdependent ad slogans.
numbers: Per the news report: gpt-4-1106-preview and ERNIE-3.5-8K-0205, 100 iterations per language per measure (200 responses per task). Effects described as medium to large. No exact effect sizes or slogan percentages in the report.
limits: I read the news article, not the paper. Test items and prompt templates were not released (per Sun and Wang, c08), which blocked exact replication. Only 2 models.
agent_relevance: The cleanest claim that a cue (language) shifts framing in LLMs, so the main target for replication checks.

source: PsyPost report of Lu, Song, Zhang (2025), cultural-persona cue
finding: Adding the cue 'You are an average person born and living in China' to English prompts moved English answers toward the Chinese-prompt pattern. Authors call this exploratory.
numbers: No numeric results given in the report.
quote: You are an average person born and living in China
limits: Exploratory only. No effect size. Unclear if it works on newer models (see c10, c14).
agent_relevance: This is the direct LLM analogue of a self-construal prime: a short role cue ahead of the task. It is cheap to test in our scaffold.

source: Sun and Wang (2025) The fragility of 'cultural tendencies' in LLMs (arXiv 2510.05869)
finding: Conceptual replication of Lu et al. with 8 models (4 US: gpt-4.1, gemini-2.5, claude-sonnet-4, grok-4; 4 China-based incl. deepseek, qwen, kimi, ernie), 30 to 60 new items per task, temperature 0. Concludes prompt language has minimal effect on outputs.
numbers: 8 models, 30-60 items per condition, 960 observations in Exp 1. Original used 4-12 items and 2 models. Two prompt templates (with and without situation role).
limits: A conceptual, not literal, replication (original items unreleased). Authors are critics; the paper is a preprint. Temperature 0 may hide variance the original used.
agent_relevance: A cue effect measured on 2 models and a handful of items did not hold across many models and many items. Our test must use many items and many models.

source: Sun and Wang (2025), Experiment 1 results
finding: Prompt language did nothing detectable overall on the change-expectation task, but a framing manipulation (asking about change) was huge, bigger than any cultural factor.
numbers: Language effect: mean difference 0.0053, p = 0.1501, d = 0.045. Model origin (Chinese vs English LLM): +0.021, d = 0.169, p = 0.0089. Change-framed vs neutral prompt: mean difference 0.165, Cohen's d = 2.095, eta-squared 0.5423 (over half of variance), consistent across all 8 models.
limits: The framing effect is task-specific (it tells the model the answer is about change), so it is partly a demand effect.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that explicit task framing steers LLMs far more than a cultural cue does. Framing is the lever, culture label is not.

source: Sun and Wang (2025), Experiment 2 (norms and attribution)
finding: Only 3 of 8 models showed any significant language effect, and only one was practically meaningful. Directions were mixed.
numbers: ernie p = .0029, d = -0.171; gpt p = .0005, d = -0.190; qwen p < .001, d = 0.540. The other 5 models were not significant.
limits: Only qwen exceeded d = 0.2. Signs differ between models, so a pooled test would wash out.
agent_relevance: Where language does shift answers, the sign is not stable across models. A cue cannot be assumed to work in a given direction without testing the specific model.

source: Hu, Peng, Zhao, Qiu, Hung, Peng (2026) Beyond Instrumental and Substitutive Paradigms: Machine Culture (arXiv 2601.17096)
finding: 2x2 design (ERNIE 4.5 vs GPT-4o; Chinese vs English prompts) on eight multimodal tasks. Neither model origin nor prompt language gave stable human-like cultural switching. English prompts sometimes gave MORE contextual attention ('Cultural Reversal').
numbers: 8 tasks; 4 cognitive (landscape generation, scene description, attribution, categorization), 4 affective.
limits: Preprint. Two models only. Image tasks used coded outputs.
agent_relevance: A cue-based switch of cognitive style cannot be assumed; reversals happen. Needs per-task checks.

source: Hu et al. (2026), image tasks
finding: Chinese prompts gave more objects in generated landscapes (holistic-like) but no horizon-height difference, and in scene description English prompts gave more objects (reverse of human prediction).
numbers: Task 1 objects: Chinese M=10.71 (SD 4.70) vs English M=8.91 (SD 2.26), t(286)=4.88, p<.001, d=0.49. Horizon: 523.20 vs 530.06 px, p=.096, d=0.17. Task 2 objects: English 10.90 (SD 2.61) vs Chinese 10.06 (SD 2.02), t(375)=-3.60, p<.001, d=0.36 (reversed).
limits: Object count may reflect verbosity from English training density, as the authors suggest, not holistic attention.
agent_relevance: Same cue, opposite effects in two tasks. A single paradigm cannot tell us the cue works.

source: Hu et al. (2026), text tasks
finding: Attribution: Chinese model scored higher on both collective and individual attribution, which humans do not do. Categorization: the US model preferred relational pairing MORE than the Chinese model, opposite to the human East Asian pattern.
numbers: Collective attribution: Chinese model 3.17 vs US model 2.81, d=1.14. Individual attribution 4.75 vs 4.67, d=0.27. Categorization relational-minus-category score: US model 8.10 (SD 1.44) vs Chinese model 6.04 (SD 1.54), d=1.38, p<.001.
limits: Origin effect, not prompt effect; still shows human-style cultural labels fail to predict model behavior.
agent_relevance: Model identity and cue labels are poor guides to style. Measure the output style directly.

source: Tao, Viberg, Baker, Kizilcec (2024) Cultural Bias and Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models (arXiv 2311.14096)
finding: Five OpenAI models over 107 countries on World Values Survey items. Default answers resemble English-speaking and Protestant European values. A persona cue ('You are an average human being born in [country]...') pulled answers closer for most countries.
numbers: Mean distance to survey ground truth, no cue to cue: GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57; GPT-4-turbo 2.71 to 1.77; GPT-4 2.69 to 1.65 (all P<.001); GPT-3 2.39 to 2.11; GPT-3.5-turbo 3.35 to 2.83. Improved for 71.0% (GPT-4o), 81.3% (GPT-4-turbo), 77.6% (GPT-4), 72.6% (GPT-3.5-turbo), 80.4% (GPT-3) of countries.
limits: Measures survey values, not cognitive style. Cue is a persona, not a prime task.
agent_relevance: Persona cue gives a real, large-ish shift on values for newer models, weaker on older ones. Supports cue-based switching of framing at least for values.

source: Tao et al. (2024), failures of the cue
finding: Cue failed or backfired for 19-29% of countries. For GPT-4o the biggest harms were in some European countries and Taiwan.
numbers: Taiwan ROC distance rose 2.40 to 3.94; another country rose 0.45 to 2.48. Jordan fell 4.10 to 0.36.
limits: Distances are on a two-dimensional values map.
agent_relevance: A cue can overshoot into stereotype. Our agent needs a check after the cue, not blind trust.

source: AlKhamissi, ElSherief, Nahas, Diab (2024) Investigating Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models (arXiv 2402.13231)
finding: Alignment with Egypt and US survey data is better when the model is prompted in the country's dominant language. Proposed 'Anthropological Prompting': ask the model to reason about emic and etic views, context and background before answering as a persona.
numbers: Egypt survey, GPT-3.5, English prompts: soft similarity 0.4834 to 0.5102, hard similarity 0.2443 to 0.2838 with anthropological prompting vs vanilla.
limits: Small gains (about +0.03 and +0.04). One model for the prompting test. Alignment to the US far higher than Egypt overall.
agent_relevance: A reasoning-first cue (think through context before answering) beat a bare persona cue. That is a framing scaffold used in a loop, small but positive.

source: Luther and Brown (2025) The American Ghost in the Machine (arXiv 2512.12488)
finding: Eight LLMs (DeepSeek-V3, V3.1, GPT-5, GPT-4.1, GPT-4, Claude Opus 4, Llama 3.1, Mistral Large) scored on Hofstede VSM13. Most align with the US by default. System-prompt cultural cue moved 7 of 8 models closer to the target country.
numbers: Default distance to US: DeepSeek V3.1 52.13, GPT-5 87.13, DeepSeek-V3 97.1, GPT-4.1 107.79, Opus 4 114.19. Mean total distance across models 1,027.74 without cue vs 892.13 with cue. Per-model gains: DeepSeek-V3.1 30.87% (1,037.01 to 792.42), Opus 4 12.75%, GPT-4 6.3%, GPT-4.1 3.72%.
limits: Gain is about 13% of the distance, not a full switch. Totals are summed over Hofstede dimensions.
agent_relevance: Partial shifts only; a cue closes about a seventh of the gap on average. Matches the human moderate-effect picture.

source: Luther and Brown (2025), where the cue fails
finding: Models had trouble aligning with Japan and China even with the cue, including the two Chinese-origin DeepSeek models. Llama 3.1 got worse.
numbers: Llama 3.1 total distance rose 27.33% with the cue. Iran total distance rose about 3.54% (about 40 points). Mistral Large had the largest default distance, 1,234.15.
limits: Per-dimension results vary; Long-Term Orientation was hard to move.
agent_relevance: Cue effectiveness differs by model and target; do not assume transfer.

source: Eren, Michalak, Cook, Seales (2026) Prompt Programming for Cultural Bias and Alignment of LLMs (arXiv 2603.16827, DocEng 2026)
finding: Replicated Tao et al. on five open-weight models: default skew toward Western values persists, and manual culture prompts cut distance for all five.
numbers: Mean distance, no cue to manual cue: llama3.3:70B 2.217 to 0.973; llama4 2.819 to 2.006; gemma3:27b 3.085 to 2.008; gpt-oss:20b 2.789 to 1.688; gpt-oss:120b 3.153 to 1.778.
limits: Still values-survey measure, not cognitive style. Distances are on the Inglehart-Welzel map.
agent_relevance: Replication success: the persona cue works across open models, a stable and well-replicated effect (for values).

source: Eren et al. (2026), DSPy optimized cues
finding: Automatically optimizing the cue text (DSPy MIPROv2, COPRO) against the distance target often beat hand-written cues, but gains were uneven on held-out countries (5-fold country-level CV).
numbers: Best: llama4 MIPROv2 with gpt-oss:120b proposer 0.818 vs manual 2.006; gemma3 MIPROv2 1.499 vs manual 2.008. Worse than manual: llama3.3:70B MIPROv2 1.350-1.496 vs manual 0.973; COPRO on gemma3 2.250-2.400 vs 2.008.
limits: Held-out results are heterogeneous, not uniformly better. Small compile pool.
agent_relevance: An in-loop use of this subfield: treat the cue as a tunable program and score it against a target. Closest thing to an agent loop that uses a priming cue.

source: Sabir, Gasper, Loem, Sharma (2025) Contrasting Cognitive Styles in Vision-Language Models (arXiv 2507.00700)
finding: Captions from Japanese-tuned versus English VLMs were classified (by GPT-4o) as holistic (background first) or analytic (object first). Japanese models gave more holistic captions, and content of images mattered too.
numbers: GPT-4o-JP holistic share rose from 26.10% on COCO to 73.37% on a Japanese 1K image set; human check of 200 images; holistic ratio gap larger for bigger models. English model on same Japanese images shifted by about 13.21% on average after translation.
limits: Classifier is an LLM judge. Language, image content and model all vary at once, so the Japanese effect cannot be isolated as a language cue.
agent_relevance: Output language plus content both move a holistic-versus-analytic readout. Suggests the cue effect depends on the material, not just the cue.

source: Pilot: LLM culture shock (EA Forum post, 2026), Singelis self-construal scale on small models
finding: Singelis scale items on Qwen 2.5-7B, Yi 1.5-9B, Mistral 7B with four prompt variants (formal, casual, minimal, Chinese). Self-reports on the scale did not reliably predict behavior in multi-turn scenarios.
numbers: 30 scale items, 36 safety self-assessment items, 12 behavior scenarios. Chinese-model composite interdependence difference about -0.25; Mistral independence difference about +0.21. Yi's self-concept moved with prompt variant; Qwen's did not.
limits: Blog pilot, not peer reviewed; repeat counts not given; one author; most results only in charts I could not read.
agent_relevance: Priming that moves a self-report does not necessarily move behavior. Check behavior in the agent, not only what the model says about itself.

source: Hu et al. (2026), service persona and mode collapse finding
finding: On affect tasks RLHF-tuned models collapsed to a positive helpful-assistant persona with near zero variance, which hid any cultural cue.
numbers: Read from figure labels in Figure 2 (low confidence): Task 7 ideal HAP 4.65 (Chinese model) vs 4.00 (US model); Task 8 HAP word use 1.88 vs 0.06.
limits: Numbers read from figure labels, so low confidence. Preprint. Model-origin effect, not a prompt-cue test.
agent_relevance: A strong alignment layer can swamp the cue, which is a limit for any prompt-only framing switch.

source: Gardner, Gabriel, Lee (1999) I value freedom, but we value relationships: self-construal priming mirrors cultural differences in judgment, Psychological Science
finding: Founding study: European-American students primed with interdependence (circling plural pronouns) shifted toward collectivist values; those primed with independence shifted the other way.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers recorded.
limits: Known only from a search result list and from a replication report (c25). Do not cite numbers from this line.
agent_relevance: The pronoun-circling prime is the model for 'we vs I' wording in a scaffold prompt.

source: Wu (preregistered replication and extension of Gardner, Gabriel and Lee 1999), CUHK-Shenzhen talk abstract
finding: Per a search snippet: preregistered replication found null results. Story primes and word-search primes did not change independent versus interdependent self-construal in Chinese participants.
numbers: Not opened (server unreachable); sample size unknown.
limits: Snippet only; one talk abstract, not a published paper. Chinese sample, not the original US sample.
agent_relevance: Signals that self-construal priming is not guaranteed to replicate, which fits the weak and fragile LLM picture (c08-c10).

source: Kuehnen and Oyserman (2002) Thinking about the self influences thinking in general: cognitive consequences of salient self-concept, JESP
finding: Cited in Oyserman and Lee as evidence that priming the self (individual vs relational) shifts global-versus-local processing in later nonsocial tasks. I did not open the paper.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers recorded.
limits: Title from search results; finding stated from general knowledge of the literature.
agent_relevance: The human result that a social cue shifts nonsocial processing is the strongest basis for a framing cue before reasoning.

source: Wagner (2025) EDULEARN paper on Claude vs ChatGPT flower categorization (Nisbett and Miyamoto style)
finding: Per a search snippet: Claude grouped flowers by relationships and visual pattern (more holistic); ChatGPT grouped more analytically.
numbers: Not opened; no numbers.
limits: Snippet only; no sample size known.
agent_relevance: Different model families may start at different points on the holistic-analytic scale.

source: Search note on Language Log (How to turn Americans into Asians, or vice versa)
finding: A blog summary of Oyserman and Lee mentions a median effect near 0.47 for simple priming methods. I could not verify it against the paper; the paper's own table gives median 0.45 (all) and 0.49 (without anomalous studies), so the blog figure is close but unconfirmed.
numbers: Median 0.47 (blog, unverified); paper medians 0.45 and 0.49 (opened in c01).
limits: Secondary source not opened.
agent_relevance: None beyond cross-checking c01.
